**What `weave.init` does (Python)**

- `weave.init()` authenticates with Weights & Biases and configures the OTel exporter. In the agent quickstart, that exporter sends agent spans to the **Agents** view [S2].
- It also sets where your traces go. The project you pass is the name Weave uses to organize your traces. Once you call `weave.init("[PROJECT_NAME]")`, the OpenAI integration automatically patches the library, so later OpenAI calls are traced [S3].
- If the project doesn't exist on your team, Weave creates it the first time you write to it [S2].
- For the agent tracing functions, call it before `start_conversation()` and similar calls. Those functions silently do nothing if the init call is absent [S4].

**What project string to pass**

You can pass either of two forms:

1. `"team-name/project-name"` logs to a specific team (the W&B entity) and project. For example, `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")`, where the team is your CoreWeave Forge team name and the project is your Weights & Biases project name [S4]. The Verdict page describes the same form for its `project` argument [S1].
2. `"project-name"` alone logs to your default team or entity [S1][S3]. For example, `weave.init("verdict_demo")` [S1].

If you're unsure, use the `team/project` form so the destination is explicit. To check or change your default entity, see User settings in the W&B docs [S3].

```python
import weave

weave.init("my-team/my-project")
```

sources.text:
## Tracing

Storing traces of LLM applications in a central database is valuable both during development and in production. Use these traces for debugging and to help build a dataset of tricky examples to evaluate against while you improve your application.

Weave can automatically capture traces for the [`openai` Python library](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries).

To start capturing, call `weave.init("[PROJECT_NAME]")` with a project name of your choice. Weave automatically patches OpenAI regardless of when you import it, so all subsequent OpenAI calls are traced.

If you don't specify a CoreWeave Forge team when you call `weave.init()`, Weave uses your default entity. To find or update your default entity, refer to [User settings](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/app/settings-page/user-settings.md#default-team) in the Weights & Biases Models documentation.

## Getting started

To enable Weave tracing for your Verdict pipelines, call `weave.init(project=...)` at the beginning of your script. Use the `project` argument to log to a specific Weights & Biases Team name with `team-name/project-name`, or pass `project-name` to log to your default team or entity.

```python lines {7} theme={"system"}
import weave
from verdict import Pipeline
from verdict.common.judge import JudgeUnit
from verdict.schema import Schema

# Initialize Weave with your project name
weave.init("verdict_demo")

# Create a simple evaluation pipeline
pipeline = Pipeline()
pipeline = pipeline >> JudgeUnit().prompt("Rate the quality of this text: {source.text}")

# Create sample data
data = Schema.of(text="This is a sample text for evaluation.")

# Run the pipeline - Weave traces this automatically
output = pipeline.run(data)

print(output)
```

## Construct object refs

Refs uniquely identify a stored object and version. The following sections describe the URI structure and the ways you can construct a ref.

In Weave, a fully qualified object ref URI looks like this:

```text theme={"system"}

## Link to a conversation from your app

To deep-link from your own UI to a conversation in the Weave Agents view, build the URL from your entity, project, and the conversation id. `weave.init()` returns a client that carries `entity` and `project`, and `start_conversation` exposes `conversation_id`.

```python lines Python theme={"system"}
from weave.trace.urls import agent_conversation_path

client = weave.init(f"{TEAM}/{PROJECT}")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="research-bot") as conversation:
    # ... run turns ...
    url = agent_conversation_path(
        client.entity, client.project, conversation.conversation_id
    )
    print(f"View this conversation at {url}")
```

## Track custom functions

LLM applications often have additional logic, such as pre-processing and post-processing, prompts, and more, that you want to track. Use this approach when you want Weave to capture your own functions alongside the LLM calls it traces automatically.

**Python**

Weave lets you manually track these Calls using the [`@weave.op`](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/reference/python-sdk#function-op) decorator. For example:

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave

# Initialize Weave Tracing
weave.init('intro-example')

# Decorate your function
@weave.op
def my_function(name: str):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# Call your function -- Weave will automatically track inputs and outputs
print(my_function("World"))
```

You can also track [methods on classes](#track-class-and-object-methods).

sources.text:
## Tracing

Storing traces of LLM applications in a central database is valuable both during development and in production. Use these traces for debugging and to help build a dataset of tricky examples to evaluate against while you improve your application.

Weave can automatically capture traces for the [`openai` Python library](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries).

To start capturing, call `weave.init("[PROJECT_NAME]")` with a project name of your choice. Weave automatically patches OpenAI regardless of when you import it, so all subsequent OpenAI calls are traced.

If you don't specify a CoreWeave Forge team when you call `weave.init()`, Weave uses your default entity. To find or update your default entity, refer to [User settings](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/app/settings-page/user-settings.md#default-team) in the Weights & Biases Models documentation.

## Getting started

To enable Weave tracing for your Verdict pipelines, call `weave.init(project=...)` at the beginning of your script. Use the `project` argument to log to a specific Weights & Biases Team name with `team-name/project-name`, or pass `project-name` to log to your default team or entity.

```python lines {7} theme={"system"}
import weave
from verdict import Pipeline
from verdict.common.judge import JudgeUnit
from verdict.schema import Schema

# Initialize Weave with your project name
weave.init("verdict_demo")

# Create a simple evaluation pipeline
pipeline = Pipeline()
pipeline = pipeline >> JudgeUnit().prompt("Rate the quality of this text: {source.text}")

# Create sample data
data = Schema.of(text="This is a sample text for evaluation.")

# Run the pipeline - Weave traces this automatically
output = pipeline.run(data)

print(output)
```

To deep-link from your own UI to a conversation in the Weave Agents view, build the URL from your entity, project, and the conversation id. `weave.init()` returns a client that carries `entity` and `project`, and `start_conversation` exposes `conversation_id`.
